_comment: Copy to config/local.json (git-ignored) and edit for this machine. Every key is optional. routes overrides the tier assignments in router.json; each target must be in router.json's models roster. Leave out models this machine does not have.
_escalation: pi workers on these models hand off after more than after_consecutive_errors failed tool calls in a row.
_rules: Send a task type a model is known to get wrong elsewhere: when the router picks a model in from and the task text matches pattern, use to. None needed now: counting went to Slotstream while Qwen3.5-4B was the standard model; Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with the prompt below gets counts right (tests/calibration/experiments.md).
_prompts: Extra system-prompt text for a model's workers, for a mistake it is known to make. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B's counting: 82% correct without, 96% with (tests/calibration/experiments.md). The second paragraph is a draft rule for summarize_files chores (explain, compare or list what named files contain): it tells the model the fact-line format that tools/qual/summarize_check.py parses exactly ("- <claim> [path:line]", one fact per line, starting with the name the fact is about; any other list item fails the reply, and so does a file and line written in any other shape or place - a bare path:N, path#LN, path line N, (line N) after a path, a bracket split over lines, in prose, a heading, a code span or a code block - a fabricated one is also counted; other lines are ignored); it is not qualified until tools/qual/summarize_run.py shows it on the holdout split (tests/calibration/experiments.md, "Summarize chores").

prompts.lmstudio/qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b:
The grep tool lists matching lines and never counts them. To answer a count, run a counting command with the bash tool (grep -c, wc -l, or jq length for JSON) and report the number it prints; do not count lines of tool output yourself.

When asked what files contain or how they differ, read every named file in full before answering. Answer with fact lines only. A fact line is one fact on one line, in exactly this form: - <claim> [path:line]. It starts with "- " and ends with one bracketed citation list, the path written in full as the task names the file, and a line number or a short range of at most 5 lines, for example: - load_config returns the defaults when the file is missing [src/config.py:41-43]. Start each fact line with the name it is about (the function, variable, class or file, as load_config starts the example; for a method, its own name), then say in words what the code does; a name or a signature alone is not a claim. Write a file and line only as the trailing [path:line] of a fact line, never in any other shape or place: no path:line, path#L, "line N" or "(line N)" in a claim, a heading, a sentence, a code span or a code block, no citation split over two lines, and no heading or "Line N" under a file name. Any other reference to a file and line fails the whole reply, even a correct one; a fact line without its own [path:line] is not counted. State only what the files say. If the files do not show something, say "not in the files" instead of guessing.

_followup: A fast local chat model judges whether a new message belongs to a running delegated task; between the two ask_between probabilities the user is asked. extra_body is added to the judge's request (LM Studio's Qwen3.6 thinks unless reasoning_effort is none). Without this key Laya judges, and asks more often (tests/calibration/experiments.md).
_packet_files: Workers on these models get up to 3 files, picked by the selector (a Claude model, via claude -p), in their context packet. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B: 52/60 chores without, 56/60 with; Slotstream gained nothing (tests/calibration/experiments.md).
_redaction: Secret redaction for tool output (docs/sensitive-read-redaction-design.md). shadow (default) keeps the per-call sensitive-read prompts and logs what redaction would do to ~/.config/tmux-pi/state/redaction/shadow.log; on redacts output with placeholders and prompts only for credential stores; off disables it. TP_REDACTION overrides.
